cost.context: ChatRepair reported $0.42 per fixed bug (ChatGPT, Defects4J, 2024). Different bugs and model; context only.

e1.takeaway: Ours reaches Recall@10 0.525 against 0.522 for the readily-available-information ranker B7 (Holm-adjusted p = 0.3823, Cliff's δ = +0.030, negligible): no measurable difference. Against failure history B4 (0.439) the adjusted p is 0.01025 and the effect is negligible (δ = +0.114); against random order (0.029) the effect is medium (δ = +0.469).
e1.test: Wilcoxon signed-rank (two-sided, zero_method=zsplit). One Holm family of 10 tests: ours vs each of the 8 baselines, plus B6 vs B4 and B7 vs B4. Cliff's delta is the first method minus the second; 'second method mean' is the Recall@10 of the second method.
e1.verdict: Gate 3 (ROADMAP §37.1) is NOT MET: on the 148 test instances the ranker's Recall@10 is 0.525 (95% bootstrap CI [0.447, 0.599]) against 0.522 for the best baseline (B7 readily-available-info LTR); Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon p = 0.3823, Cliff's delta = +0.030 (negligible). The criterion is: higher mean, adjusted p < 0.05 and |delta| >= 0.147.

e3.applier_note: The E3 evaluation uses a strict patch applier (exact match), while the PR bot uses a whitespace-tolerant applier; E3 fix rates are therefore conservative relative to the bot.

e1.candidates_median: B1 (random, mean over 20 seeds, std over those 20) is the floor; B4 has no randomness. Candidate test files per test instance: median 595, max 3079.

e3_detection.takeaway: On fresh repositories with no failure history the E1 order puts the first failing file at mean position 10.91, behind alphabetical order (8.11) and level with random (10.37); by mean share of files run first it is ahead of alphabetical (0.485 vs 0.553). The strongest signal, failure history, does not exist on a fresh repository.
